liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancing In The Streets** (2 reviews): The opening song was an awesome surprise, though excitement waned as mud deepened; The band opened with a ripping version of this song, keeping the energy high [20][25]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): This version was very high powered, featuring a hot Jerry jam [28]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ramble On Rose**: cut on the recording [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-24.132577.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 152 min [1]
- **gd1984-06-24.sbd.miller.27449.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 3.75/5 by 20 [3]
- **gd84-06-24.nak.connor.4628.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 148 min; rated 3.83/5 by 23 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds great streaming, though audience noise is prominent during quiet sections; Bass lacks definition, but the second set features definitive, expressive performances [18][19]
- **gd1984-06-24.165037.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min [7]
- **gd1984-06-24.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81627.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 154 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [10]

## Around the show

- Heavy rain and deep mud made the audience worry about drowning during the show [20]
- Bobby sprinted across the stage during Bertha while Billy bashed his drum kit [21]
- The band broke SPAC attendance records with roughly 35,000 to 38,000 people [24]
- Fans camped out at Saratoga, enduring heavy rain and mud splashing under their shoes [25]
- The reviewer danced continuously all night, recalling a tent along the road at the hilltop [26]
- Security held the concrete walkways until halfway through Hell In A Bucket before the crowd broke through [29]
- This Deal performance has flubs and does not match the June 1985 Greek Theatre version [28]
- Dancin' In The Streets had not been played since July 7, 1981, a 203-show gap [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-24.132577.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; Nakamichi CM100/CP4 Shotguns > Sony D5, Tapes:Maxell UDXLII 90's; Tapes Labelled:Nakamichi 100 Guns -… [1]. Also: Steve recorded the source; the Hill collection provided masters with tape pauses in the first set [1]
- **gd1984-06-24.sbd.miller.27449.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [3]. Also: Nakamichi 300 with CP1 microphone created a cassette master, later transferred to DAT [3]
- **gd84-06-24.nak.connor.4628.sbeok.shnf**: source: Aud> Nak300> CM> CDR> EAC(Secure Mode)> CDWave(Retracking Only)> Shnv3(MKW ACT) [4]
- **gd1984-06-24.165037.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [7]
- **gd1984-06-24.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81627.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Tim Burke; source: Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90 (No Dolby) [10]. Also: Beyer M88 microphone recorded the show; tape flips occurred during several songs [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 6/24/1984 Saratoga Springs NY Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_840624.html) [31]
- Poster by Steven Rood Grateful Dead: [1984-06-24 Saratoga Performing Arts Center, Saratoga Springs, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-06-24-saratoga-performing-arts-center-saratoga-springs-ny-usa/) [32]
